title: Max your Solo 401(k) (or SEP-IRA)
summary: Employee deferral up to $24,500 plus employer profit-sharing (~20% of net SE earnings as a sole prop; 25% of W-2 wages for corp owner-employees).
detailsHtml:
The employer-side math

For a sole proprietor or single-member LLC taxed as a sole proprietor, the "employer" contribution under IRC §404 follows a circular formula: contribution = (net SE income − ½ SE tax − contribution) × 25%. Solving the circularity yields an effective rate of approximately 20% of net SE income. For an S-corp owner-employee, the formula is cleaner: 25% of W-2 wages, with no circularity. The effective optimization depends on entity structure (addressed in Phase 9). For Solo 401(k) providers, most calculators handle the circular math automatically — but understanding the source of the ~20% effective rate matters when comparing entity structures.

Sole prop, $200K net SE income: Half SE tax deduction: ~$10,000 Adjusted net income: ~$190,000 Employer contribution cap: 20% × $190K = $38,000 Plus employee deferral: $24,500 Total Solo 401(k) cap: $62,500 (Up to $72,000 absolute cap for 2026)

Solo defined benefit plans for very high earners

Contractors with consistent $300K+ net income can layer a defined benefit (cash balance) plan on top of a Solo 401(k), enabling total contributions of $100,000–$300,000+ per year. Complex and expensive to administer ($3,000–$5,000/year), but the tax savings can be enormous at top brackets.
